input.prompt:
Create a 15-second, 9:16, photorealistic handheld phone video in one continuous shot.

REFERENCE ROLES
Image 1 is the sole identity reference for the lead person: preserve that person's facial structure, hairstyle, skin tone and visible outfit. Use no identity features from any other person. Image 2 is the environment and supporting-cast reference. Insert the lead into its empty central standing space, behind the foreground phone-holder and in front of the background people. Keep the lead visible from roughly waist or chest level upward as the foreground allows.

SCENE AND CAMERA
A close, crowded encounter at a red-lit entrance beside a staircase. Keep the diagonal stair railing and pale column toward the left and back, and the strongly red-lit vertical doorway and wall toward the right. Preserve the black-clothed supporting people from Image 2. A curly-haired person in a dark plum hoodie stands in the lower-right foreground, back and shoulder toward the camera, holding a vertical smartphone and a black portable speaker with a circular end cap. Preserve these foreground occlusions: the lead stands behind them. The phone remains a phone and the speaker remains a portable speaker. Keep the candid phone-camera exposure, red spill light, natural skin texture, slight handheld jitter and small framing corrections.

PERFORMANCE TIMELINE
0-1.2 s: The lead looks toward the camera area, left elbow bent, left hand near the upper chest or chin. Loosely gathered fingertips make small expressive movements.
1.2-2.0 s: The lead turns the head and upper body slightly toward their own right, toward screen-left. The left hand opens across the chest, then the lead turns back toward the camera area.
2.0-7.0 s: Continue compact left-hand gestures between chest and face height, alternating an open palm with loosely gathered fingertips. Add gentle shoulder motion, brief head turns and occasional smiles.
7.0-8.5 s: Lower the chin, dip the shoulders slightly and lower the left hand.
8.5-9.5 s: Raise the left hand again toward the side of the face.
9.5-11.0 s: With the elbow bent, raise the LEFT forearm almost vertically in front of the face. The hand reaches forehead height or slightly above it. Make a small wrist rotation. The clearest high-arm pose occurs around 10-11 s; the hand briefly overlaps part of the face.
11.0-11.5 s: Lower the left arm and tilt the head downward.
11.5-15.0 s: Return to small shoulder bounces and compact gestures between chest and waist height, looking mostly downward with occasional smiles.

AUDIO AND MOUTH MOVEMENT
Use reference Audio 1 as the timing and vocal-phrasing guide. Follow its existing Spanish vocal delivery, pauses, rhythmic backing and ambient texture as closely as possible. Align the lead's visible mouth movements to the audible lead-vocal phrases, relaxing or smiling during pauses. Do not invent additional lines, translate the words, change the musical arrangement or add narration. The reference audio will also be used for final soundtrack replacement after generation.

CONSISTENCY
Keep the lead's identity and outfit consistent during head turns and hand occlusion. Supporting people may smile or make small natural movements while keeping their identities, clothes and general places. Keep the spatial layering stable. Do not add a cut, a new location, a full-body dance routine, repeated clapping, extra limbs, a portrait on the phone display, subtitles or a watermark.

OPTIONAL IMAGE 3
Image 3 is only a pose and body-orientation guide for the 10-11 s high-arm moment. Replace its gray mannequin completely with the real lead from Image 1. Do not copy its gray material, featureless face, hairstyle, clothes or skin appearance. Do not introduce a second lead or a mannequin into the video. Image 1 remains the sole lead identity and outfit reference.
